public_rationale: This is a rhetorical description of why big tech and its investors embrace generative AI. It turns on claims about motives: that investors back companies for 'signals' to speculators rather than for products for real people. It names no company, period, or measure. Big tech plainly talks up AI growth to investors, but that would not separate the speaker's reading from ordinary business strategy. No fair plain reading yields a true-or-false test, so the claim is not scored.
limitations: One screen suggested checking investor presentations. They could show that firms pitch AI as growth, but not the motives the claim centers on.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: For big tech, generative AI is mainly a growth story for investors and Wall Street speculators.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI is catnip for big tech — a narratively-satisfying way of expressing how big their companies will grow for investors that don't invest in companies because they make things for real people, but for the signals they issue to Wall Street speculators.

our_interpretation: This is a description of the motives of big tech firms and their investors, framed as rhetoric. It sets no measurable quantity or threshold.

That companies pitch AI as a growth story to investors can be observed. But the claim's real content is that investors care about signals rather than products. That is a judgment about motives, and no public evidence could cleanly confirm or refute it.
